turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I feel like I’m worrying about everything lately. My clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just feels bigger than it should, compared to what’s actually going on.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports worrying about multiple areas of life and says the worry feels disproportionate to current circumstances.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any changes in your body, like tension or restlessness, when you're worrying?
turns.patient_response: Yes. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders get really tight, like I’ve been bracing myself all day. And I’ve noticed I clench my jaw sometimes, especially when I’m driving between listings or sitting at my desk.

symptom_reasoning.S061: The patient reports end-of-day neck and shoulder tightness and jaw clenching during driving or desk work.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been avoiding any activities or situations because of your worries?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d say I avoid things, exactly. I still go to work and meet clients and handle what I need to. Sometimes I might put off making a call or checking something if I’m already worked up, but I don’t think I’ve been avoiding whole situations because of it.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient states they have not been avoiding whole situations because of their worries, while describing only occasional procrastination when already worked up.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I get stressed and overwhelmed, but I wouldn’t say I feel sad or down most of the time.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient states they would not say they feel sad or down most of the time.

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any episodes where you suddenly felt intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think so. I get worried and tense, but I can’t remember having a sudden wave of intense fear like that that peaks within a few minutes.

turns.doctor_question: Has your worrying been affecting your performance at work or your relationships with family and friends?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think it has, mostly at work. Things that used to be pretty straightforward, like listing negotiations or reviewing contracts, are taking me a lot longer now. I’ll keep checking things over because I don’t feel sure I’ve caught everything, and sometimes I delay returning calls because of that.

symptom_reasoning.functional_impairment: The patient reports that work tasks are taking much longer and that worry-driven repeated checking causes delayed return calls.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been worrying about being judged or evaluated by others?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t really notice myself worrying specifically about being judged or evaluated. It’s more just general worry, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient describes their experience as 'general worry,' supporting the presence of worry without specifying its scope, severity, or controllability.

turns.doctor_question: Is your worrying mostly about one particular thing or are you worrying about a wide range of things?
turns.patient_response: It’s definitely a wide range of things. I worry about clients, the market, my family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just feels like it’s more worry than the situation really calls for.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports excessive worry across multiple domains (clients, market, family, money, housing decision) and states it is out of proportion to the circumstances.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?
turns.patient_response: I haven’t really noticed being more tired than usual. I mean, I have normal tired days, but nothing that stands out to me lately.

symptom_reasoning.S029: The patient states they have not noticed being more tired than usual and reports only normal tired days.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself having recurring, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
turns.patient_response: Yes, sometimes. It’s not like one strange thought over and over, but I’ll tell myself, “Parin, this isn’t urgent,” and then one concern leads into another. Before I know it, I’ve spent half an hour going back over little details I meant to just let go.

symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient describes concerns chaining into one another and spending prolonged time replaying details despite trying to dismiss them, indicating difficulty controlling worry.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your worrying is interfering with your overall quality of life?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think it is, at least at work. Even straightforward listing negotiations or reviewing contracts are taking me much longer than they used to. I’ll put off returning calls sometimes because I don’t feel confident that I’ve checked everything carefully enough. It’s not completely stopping me, but it does slow me down.

symptom_reasoning.S057: Worry leads the patient to repeatedly check work carefully enough and delay returning calls, slowing occupational functioning.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you're worrying almost every day?
turns.patient_response: Yes, pretty much almost every day. I came in because it feels like I’m worrying about everything now—clients, the market, my family, money, even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It just seems out of proportion to what’s actually happening.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports worrying almost every day about multiple areas of life and describes the worry as out of proportion to actual circumstances.

turns.doctor_question: Do you typically find it difficult to control your worry once it starts?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I do. I’ll try to tell myself, Parin, this isn’t urgent, just leave it alone, but then my mind jumps to the next concern. Before I realize it, I’ve spent half an hour going over some small detail I was trying to let go.

symptom_reasoning.S057: The patient reports that once worry begins, it chains from one concern to another and occupies about half an hour despite attempts to stop it.

turns.doctor_question: Are most of your worries about relatively minor or everyday things?
turns.patient_response: Yes, a lot of them are ordinary things. It’s clients, the market, family, money… even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. None of it is usually an emergency, but I react to it like it’s much bigger than it really is.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms worrying about multiple ordinary, non-emergency areas of life and reacting as though they are much bigger than they are.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel like your worrying is causing you a lot of distress?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s been upsetting, honestly. I came in because it feels like I’m worrying about everything now—clients, the market, my family, money, even whether moving to the condo was the right decision. And I know some of it is just everyday stuff, but it feels bigger than it should.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports worrying about multiple areas of life and says the worry feels upsetting and larger than it should.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling restless?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed being especially restless physically. It’s more that my mind feels hard to settle sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been worrying about these everyday things for more than 6 months?
turns.patient_response: Yes. It’s been more than six months. I’d say about a year and a couple months now—really since after I sold my longtime house and moved into the condo.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient confirms that worry about everyday things has persisted for more than six months, estimating about one year and two months.

turns.doctor_question: Has your worrying been affecting your relationships with family and friends outside of work?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure that it’s really affected those relationships much. I don’t think my family or friends would say I’ve changed a lot. I may bring up worries sometimes, but I haven’t noticed any major problems with them because of it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you typically worry about these things even when everything is going well?
turns.patient_response: Yes, I think so. Even when things are basically going fine, I still find myself worrying—about clients, the market, my family, money, and whether moving to the condo was the right decision. It feels like more worry than the situation really calls for.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient reports worrying across multiple areas even when things are going well and describes the worry as disproportionate to circumstances.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I get worried and tense, but I haven’t noticed a sudden rush of intense fear that peaks like that within a few minutes.
